# Dropnook

> Dropnook is free, open-source, self-hosted instant sharing for the home network — like AirDrop, but for every device and every operating system. Text fields, files of any size and screenshots (Ctrl+V) appear live on every phone, tablet and computer in the network, in the browser: no app, no login, no cloud. Single files or texts can be shared to the internet through expiring links, optionally with a password, served by a separate locked-down container. Made for Unraid (Docker Compose via the Compose Manager Plus plugin); runs on any Linux host with Docker Compose. License: AGPL-3.0. On the devices the page is simply called "Drop" (e.g. "Tower Drop", after the server's name).

Key facts:

- Two containers from one image (ghcr.io/dropnook/dropnook): `drop` (the drop box, LAN only, refuses anything coming through a proxy) and `drop-share` (share links only; non-root, read-only file system, no Linux capabilities, sees only the shared items).
- Share links look like https://drop-share.yourdomain.com/k7m3x-9pq2r — 10 characters, no look-alike characters, about 50 bits; they expire after 15 minutes to 30 days.
- HTTPS in the LAN with an existing certificate (e.g. from Nginx Proxy Manager), found automatically.
- Picture previews, a large view and "Copy" of a picture into another computer's clipboard.
- 17 languages; five colour layouts (teal, gold, blue, violet, coral), each in light and dark.
- Optional: one PIN for everyone, or up to five users (USER_<COLOUR>: "name:PIN"), each with an area of their own next to the shared one and their own colour.
- Images are tested against a set of attacks before every release and rebuilt weekly for security updates.
